title: upgrade: FlashAttentionV2 kernels + rope/rotary fused ops + KV batching & scheduling
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: upgrade the attention execution path to FlashAttentionV2 and add a set of fused ops for rotary/rope positional transforms to eliminate extra memory copies. Additionally introduce a workload-aware KV batching and scheduling heuristic to reduce p99 latency on mixed short/long context workloads. This PR is the culmination of the ENG-4211 performance spike investigation and implements: (1) FlashAttentionV2 kernels with a compatibility shim, (2) fused rotary/rope transformations that are selected at runtime based on model config to avoid branching in the hot path, (3) fused KV-copy-reduction paths that reduce intermediate buffer allocations, and (4) a new scheduler heuristic that chooses batch size / micro-batching and KV cache placement by observing sequence-length distribution and model latency profiles. Summary of changes and rationale: - Replace legacy attention calls with FlashAttentionV2 wrappers when the device and model meet kernel constraints (smaller memory footprint, improved kernel utilization). Fallback to previous kernels on unsupported hardware. - Add fused_rope and fused_rotary ops that execute in the same CUDA kernel as attention where possible, eliminating a device <-> device memcpy. These ops were carefully validated against numeric baselines (FP16) and unit tests added. - Implement continuous KV-batching path that can combine multiple small KV writes and issue fewer CUDA kernels for KV materialization; includes an adaptive policy that favors lower latency for short contexts and higher throughput for long contexts. - Introduce scheduling heuristics: a) seq-length histogram collector (samples per route) b) policy that adjusts micro-batch size and KV batching window c) dynamic fallback thresholds to trade latency vs throughput. - Add microbenchmarks and a perf-canary job to guard regressions. Results: benchmarked on a 4xA100 node with OpenModelZoo LLMs; compared to main before this PR: median throughput +18% on long-context runs, p99 latency reduced 12-18% on mixed workloads, steady-state memory usage reduced ~6% on large models. Testing: unit tests, GPU integration tests on the CI matrix, and manual canary runs. Compatibility: no API changes. The scheduler and kernel selection are opt-in behind config flags (defaults enabled for supported hardware). Rollout plan: merged to main; will stage to perf canary pool for 48h then tag for Dedicated nodes. See linked Linear tasks for performance monitoring and rollout checklist.

perf(attn): fused rotary/rope transforms into attention kernel where supported
perf(kv): continuous KV batching + reduce-copy execution path
perf(scheduler): add seq-length histogram collector and adaptive policy
test(perf): add microbenchmarks and perf-canary job
ci: add kernel compatibility matrix and GPU test matrix
docs: upgrade notes for FlashAttentionV2 and rollout guidance
review_comments: Marco Hernandez (2024-11-09): Great work. A few quick asks: 1) add a numeric baseline test for FP16 rotary vs fused_rope, 2) guard the new kernel selection behind a config flag for Dedicated rollout, 3) verify behavior on Ampere vs Hopper.
Aisha Patel (2024-11-09): Added FP16 numeric baseline test and config flag. Ampere/Hopper compatibility matrix added to ci/gpu_matrix.yml.
Jin Soo Park (2024-11-12): The fused_rope ops look good but we should avoid extra branching in the hot path. Can we hoist config checks to module init?
Aisha Patel (2024-11-12): Moved detection to startup; runtime checks now just consult a 1-byte capability flag to avoid branches in the kernel entry path.

Elena Kuznetsova (2024-11-15): Memory accounting looks plausible but we should ensure the KV batching window doesn't cause increased tail latency under high queueing. Please add a backpressure cutoff.
Aisha Patel (2024-11-16): Added backpressure cutoff and added a canary test that simulates high arrival rates. Perf canary results attached.
Marco Hernandez (2024-11-18): CI green and perf canary shows expected improvements. Approving for squash-merge.
ci_checks: perf-canary: pass (p99 improved 12-18% on mixed workloads)
release_notes: Upgrade attention kernels to FlashAttentionV2 with fused rotary/rope ops: improved throughput and lower p99 latency on long contexts.
Introduce continuous KV batching and adaptive scheduling heuristics: better tail latency on mixed workloads and reduced kernel overhead for many small requests.
Default rollout is enabled for supported hardware; opt-out via runtime.attn.enable_flashattn_v2=false in config.
